completion.content:

What is the difference between eBGP and iBGP?

completion.content: eBGP exchanges routes between different autonomous systems. iBGP distributes BGP routes between routers inside the same AS. They also differ in default loop-prevention and route-propagation behavior.

What is MTU and why can an MTU mismatch be difficult to troubleshoot?

completion.content: MTU is the largest packet or frame size a link or interface accepts without fragmentation or rejection. A mismatch can be subtle because small control packets may work while larger application packets fail, fragment, or are dropped.

What is anycast gateway in an EVPN/VXLAN fabric?

completion.content: An anycast gateway presents the same default-gateway IP and MAC on multiple leaf switches so hosts can use a local first-hop gateway regardless of which leaf they attach to. This supports distributed routing and host mobility.

Two OSPF routers are directly connected but remain in 2-Way state on an Ethernet segment. Is that always a fault?

completion.content: No. On a broadcast Ethernet network, DROTHER routers can remain 2-Way with each other and form full adjacencies with the DR and BDR. Verify the interface network type and DR/BDR roles before treating 2-Way as a fault.

Why is longest-prefix match important in IP forwarding?

completion.content: When multiple routes match a destination, longest-prefix match selects the route with the most specific matching prefix. For example, a /24 match is preferred over a /16 match for an address contained in both.

What is an SVI?

completion.content: A switched virtual interface is a logical Layer 3 interface associated with a VLAN on a multilayer switch. It is commonly used as the default gateway for hosts in that VLAN or for switch management.
